title: Dual-Format Heading Extraction for HTML and Markdown Reports
description: This tour walks through the CLI changes made to support HTML-format library reports in the `hlx library show` command. Previously, the CLI only extracted headings from Markdown reports using a `#`-prefix regex. Since reports are switching to HTML format, the heading extraction in `src/library/show.ts` was updated to try an HTML heading regex first and fall back to the original Markdown regex for backward compatibility. No new runtime dependencies were introduced — the CLI maintains its zero-dependency design constraint. The tour follows data flow order: type extension, then heading extraction logic, then the Markdown fallback.

steps.description: The `hlx library show` command is the only place in the CLI that parses report content to extract headings. Commands like `comments-list.ts` and `comments-post.ts` are format-agnostic — they operate on anchor strings passed via `--section` and never inspect report content. Therefore, only `show.ts` needed updating. The diagnosis confirmed this narrow scope: the Markdown heading regex on line 46 (pre-change) was the single format-dependent code path in the entire CLI.
steps.title: Overview: Why show.ts Is the Only File Changed

steps.description: The local `LibraryItemDetail` type is extended with an optional `filePath?: string | null` field. The server (helix-global-server) now includes `filePath` in the library item API response to indicate whether a report is HTML or Markdown. Adding it here as optional preserves full backward compatibility — existing code paths that don't supply `filePath` continue to work. Content inspection via regex is the primary format-detection method; `filePath` is available for future use or supplementary detection.
steps.title: Step L1: Add filePath to Local LibraryItemDetail Type

steps.description: The HTML heading regex `/<h([1-6])(?:\s+[^>]*?id="([^"]*)"[^>]*)?>(.+?)<\/h\1>/i` is tried first on each line of report content. It extracts three capture groups: (1) heading level 1–6, (2) the `id` attribute value when present, and (3) the raw inner text including any nested HTML tags. When the `id` attribute is present — which is always the case for headings generated by the updated agent prompts — it is used directly as the slug anchor, avoiding any discrepancy between client-side and CLI `slugify()` implementations. A full HTML parsing library was deliberately not added; the CLI has zero runtime dependencies by design and a single regex is sufficient for well-formed `<h1>`–`<h6>` tags.
steps.title: Step L2: HTML Heading Regex (Primary Pattern)

steps.description: After the HTML regex matches, any nested HTML tags inside the heading content (e.g. `<strong>`, `<em>`, `<code>`) are stripped using `.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, '')` to produce a clean display string. This is important because the raw captured text from group 3 may contain inline markup. The cleaned text is used for display; the slug comes from the captured `id` attribute (or `slugify(rawText)` as fallback when `id` is absent).
steps.title: Stripping Nested HTML Tags from Heading Text

steps.description: After a successful HTML heading match is processed, a `continue` statement skips the rest of the loop body for that line. This ensures the same line is never evaluated by the Markdown fallback regex below. Without this guard, a line containing an HTML heading could theoretically also be tested against the Markdown `#`-prefix pattern, producing incorrect output. This is a critical correctness detail for the dual-regex design.
steps.title: continue After HTML Match Prevents Double-Processing

steps.description: The original Markdown heading regex `/^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/` is preserved completely unchanged and now serves as the fallback path. It only executes for lines that did not match the HTML pattern (enforced by the `continue` above). This ensures full backward compatibility: existing Markdown reports continue to display correctly with no behavior change. The implementation plan required this as an explicit success criterion — the Markdown regex must be bit-for-bit identical to the pre-change version.
steps.title: Step L2 (continued): Markdown Heading Regex (Fallback — Unchanged)

steps.description: Both the HTML and Markdown branches produce output in the same format: heading level indicator, display text, slug annotation, and comment count. Downstream code that renders the heading list or passes anchors to `comments-list` and `comments-post` requires no changes because the output contract is identical regardless of which regex matched. The major code paths — comment listing, comment posting, and report display — remain clean. TypeScript compilation passes with zero errors (`npx tsc --noEmit`), confirming no type regressions were introduced.
steps.title: Summary: Unified Output Format for Both Heading Types
